title: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Console I/O Operations
sourceFile: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Console I_O Operations - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# Questions and Answers focuses on "Introduction of Console I/O operations".

questions.question: Which class provides the operation of reading from and writing to the console in C#.NET?
questions.explanation: The System.Console class provides access to the standard input, output, and error streams for console applications.

questions.question: Which property of the Console class provides access to the standard output stream by default?
questions.explanation: Console.Out is a TextWriter that sends output to the screen. It is the underlying stream used by Console.Write and Console.WriteLine.

questions.question: Which property of the Console class provides access to the standard input stream?
questions.explanation: Console.In is an instance of TextReader used to read input from the keyboard (standard input).

questions.question: How many primary methods for reading input are commonly provided by the Console class?
questions.explanation: The three primary methods are Read() (reads a single character), ReadLine() (reads a line of text), and ReadKey() (reads the next pressed key).

questions.question: Select the correct input methods provided by the Console class:
questions.explanation: Read() and ReadLine() have been available since .NET 1.0, while ReadKey() was added in .NET 2.0 to handle individual key presses. ReadKey() belongs to Console, not to TextReader (Console.In).

questions.question: What is the return type of the Console.Read() method?
questions.explanation: Console.Read() returns the next character from the input stream as an 'int'. It returns -1 if no characters are available.

questions.question: What value does Console.Read() return when the end of the input stream is reached?
questions.explanation: Console.Read() returns -1 when there are no more characters to read (end of stream). An I/O failure throws IOException instead of returning -1.

questions.question: Which of the following is an instance of the TextReader class?
questions.explanation: Console.In is a property of type TextReader, which handles character-based input.

questions.question: Which property/properties of the Console class are instances of the TextWriter class?
questions.explanation: Both Console.Out and Console.Error are TextWriter objects, used for standard output and standard error respectively.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text:
Generating exception:
Attempted to divide by zero.

questions.explanation: The code first prints a string to Console.Out. Then, the division by zero triggers a catch block that prints the error message to Console.Error.

questions.question: Which methods are provided by the TextWriter objects (Console.Out and Console.Error)?
questions.explanation: TextWriter classes provide Write() (output without a newline) and WriteLine() (output followed by a newline).

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: Runs successfully but does not print anything
Asks for input and displays the square of the number

questions.explanation: The code reads a string, converts it to an integer using Convert.ToInt32, calculates the square, and prints the result.
